Shown from the knees up, a woman stands facing and looking at us with her head tilted a little to our left in this vertical portrait painting. She has pale skin, a heart-shaped face with rosy cheeks, and a rose-pink bow mouth. Thin, arched, sable-brown eyebrows frame her gray eyes. A wreath of pale pink flowers and curling white ostrich feathers crowns her long gray hair, which is piled high on her head. Loose curly tendrils brush both shoulders. Her glowing, silver satin gown is trimmed with delicate sheer lace around the wide, plunging neckline and sleeves, and has a pink sash around her narrow waist. Pearl bracelets adorn her wrists. She leans to her left, our right, to rest her left elbow against a waist-high, cinnamon-brown stone pedestal, which is decorated with a bronze-colored garland and bow on the side facing us. A ring of blue, yellow, red, and pink flowers, woven with strands of ivy, dangles in the hand resting on the pedestal. Her right hand hangs loosely by her side. Along the left edge of the dimly lit background, a tree with a thick trunk angles into the upper left corner. A smaller sapling grows just in front of it. On the right, bushes with olive and fern-green leaves dotted with lilac-purple flecks rise above the pedestal. Dark clouds fill most of the top third of the canvas but they part around her head to reveal the soft blue sky. The artist signed and dated the work in white in the lower right corner, “L. Vigée Le Brun 1782.”

About two dozen men, women, children, and a baby sit in rows of wooden benches or on traveling trunks in this horizontal painting. Their skin is mostly pale with some ranging more toward pink and others toward tan. A woman nursing a baby sits in the center of the composition. Her blond hair is pulled back, and she wears a white blouse under a red vest and a long black skirt. Her shirt is pulled down to expose one breast, and the feeding baby wears a white bonnet and clothing, and is wrapped in a gray-patterned blanket. The woman sits on a wooden trunk in front of a young girl, who sits on a second chest just behind her and to our left. This girl has strawberry blond hair held back under a black headband, and she wears a blue shawl over a brick-red dress. Three silver pans, a silver jug, a glass bottle, and tin cup sit next to her trunk. She leans forward and looks intently off to our left. A man with a red beard wears glasses, a brown suit, and a flat-topped straw hat sits farther back in the room on the far side of bulging sacks and more trunks. He looks into the distance off to our right. Three men wearing black suits and two wearing black bowler hats sit facing each other just over this man’s shoulder. In the right two-thirds of the painting, more men wear fedoras, bowler hats, or brimless caps. Their clothing ranges from vests over button-down shirts to suits and ties. Some wear overcoats, and some are bearded. One man wears a military-style hat, a double-breasted black coat, and smokes a pipe with a white bowl. He looks toward the nursing woman, as does a standing man farther in the room. The men sit alone or chat in groups of two or three, and one sleeps, propped up against a fabric bag. A few more women are among the group, including one older woman who wears a yellow scarf tied over her head to the left. A sign hanging on a column behind the nursing woman begins with the text, “Emigrant Landing Depot” over columns of fine print. The walls of the room are mottled fog and cream white, and one visible window is small within the thick wall. The floor is wooden planks and there is a brown stain near the lower right corner.

This horizontal landscape painting shows a panoramic view of a river valley and an encampment from an elevated vantage point. The horizon runs about halfway up the composition beneath a wide expanse of pale blue sky dotted with a few puffy white clouds. A rocky bluff runs along the bottom edge of the canvas, closest to us. Three people in uniforms of dark blue jackets and lighter blue pants sit or stand among the sparce trees and shrubs there. One faces away from us, one sits on a boulder and smokes a pipe, and one gestures across the river. On a flat surface a bit farther down and to the right, more people stand among six white tents. Some tend to two cannons aimed across the river, which creates a hairpin turn in the lower left corner of the composition. The wide river feeds the turn to the right and the waterway continues to the horizon to the left. What first appears to be gentle rapids on the river could be two canoes rowed by several people each. On the far side of the river are a town with buildings set loosely within a block and a road traveling into the distance, which is also lined with houses and buildings. To the right of this are a few clusters of white tents leading back to rows of countless white tents on a gently rolling hill in the distance. The tents and hills become hazy as they approach the horizon. Two piles of cream-white clouds drift across the pale blue sky above.

Dance under the Trees at the Edge of the Lake

We look across a grassy expanse leading to a lake, with several women, tiny in scale, dancing under a grove of trees to our right in this horizontal landscape painting. Painted with soft, almost feathery brushstrokes of fern and moss green to suggest leaves, two massive trees nearly fill the right half of the composition. Three light-skinned women wearing voluminous togas over one shoulder link hands in a circle beneath the tree, near the lower center of the painting. Lit by the low sun, the woman to our left wears rose pink, the center woman shimmering yellow, and the third woman emerald green. Another women to our left, wearing sapphire blue, runs toward the trio with arms outstretched. A fifth woman wearing a scarlet-red skirt reclines near the tree trunks to our right. A low, rectangular box about the length of a dining room table sits on the grass between the trio and the reclining woman. A few brushstrokes suggest flowers or plants on the box. The lake beyond is painted with smooth strokes of pale apricot and shell pink. A bank of bushes or tall vegetation close to us to our left is painted with touches of forest and olive green, with pale yellow to capture light glinting off the uppermost leaves. Beyond it, and hazy in the distance to our left, a large white building is nestled high on a hill painted in tones of muted plum purple and flaxen gold. Pale, fawn-brown hills lead down to the water in the distance, farther back along the lake. A few thin clouds float in the ice-blue sky above. The scene is loosely painted with visible brushstrokes and touches, so some details are difficult to make out. The artist signed the work in the lower left corner: “COROT.”

A nearly nude woman is carved from cream-white marble in this freestanding sculpture. In this photograph, her body faces us, and she looks to our right in profile. She has a sloping forehead and straight nose, full, closed lips, and a rounded chin. Her curly hair is pulled back but ringlets fall down the back of her neck, and tendrils curl alongside her ears. She holds her left arm, to our right, across her torso so that hand brushes her right breast. She holds drapery to her groin with the other hand, and the cloth puddles behind her feet. She steps slightly forward onto her right leg but her knees are together so the toes of her left foot brush the round, disk-like base on which she stands. The background fades from nickel gray across the top to fog gray along the bottom.

This horizontal painting is tightly packed with colorfully dressed groups of soldiers and knights on horseback surging toward each other. The scene is created with small areas of vivid, mostly flat color, almost like a collage. Long lances and spears create a forest of diagonals among the battling men. The hands and the few faces we can see are painted with pale, peachy skin. The soldiers on the left side wear tunics and leggings in tones of pumpkin orange, sage green, rose pink, ruby red, or azure blue. Most wear pointed, silver helmets with wide brims, and many hold lances as they charge the knights to our right. Near an ash-gray tree in the upper left, a rust-brown horse rears up among the throng, as his rider leans back and pulls on the reins. One person has been lifted off the ground while trying to hold the horse’s bridle. More knights on horseback sweep in from the right wearing silver armor, and riding gray, saffron orange, or brown horses. Several aim carrot-orange lances wrapped with white stripes at the enemy. The horses lunge forward with gaping mouths and wide eyes, their front legs outstretched. A band of knights in the distance in the upper right hold butter-yellow, celery-green, powder-blue, and white pennants that snap in the wind. The blue sky above the battle is scattered with white clouds on the right that transition to darker, tan clouds on the left. The artist signed the lower left corner, “M. Boutet de Monvel.”

One person with brown skin lies on a patterned carpet and a nude woman, also with brown skin, stoops and holds a white cloth to her thighs in this loosely painted horizontal scene. A wall, painted with streaks and smudges of fog gray, white, and pale peach, spans the right two-thirds of the composition behind the people. In the leftmost third, a room bumps back in space, and an arched window there opens onto a view painted with strokes of shamrock green. We may be in a courtyard or another kind of brightly lit, enclosed space. The rug is loosely painted with visible dashes and dabs of raspberry pink, sapphire blue, mint green, pale yellow, white, and brown. The person lying on the rug is angled away from us, so the bare feet are closest, near the front left corner of the rug, and the head angles to our right, near the wall. That person is wrapped with white fabric over the head and chest, lemon-yellow fabric across the middle, and emerald green over the thighs. One ankle rests over the other, and the eye we see is closed. The nude woman stands just to our right, near the front right corner of the rug. Her black hair is short or pulled up. Dabs of gold around her neck suggest a coin-like necklace or large, round beads. Her full breasts hang as she holds the white cloth to her legs. The cloth is painted with short diagonal strokes, which cascade down her right leg, to our left, and pool on the floor. The toes of the foot we can see rest on the back of a pointed shoe painted with butter yellow and black. The other shoe sits just off the front edge of the rug, near the pooled white fabric. A side table with an octagonal top is at the back right corner of the rug, and is painted with crimson red, black, white, slate blue, and harvest gold. One orange is on the floor near the white fabric, and three more are near the back left corner of the carpet. A parrot, painted with an azure-blue body, white around the eye, a marigold-orange neck, and a pointed black beak, nibbles at an open orange on the floor nearby. A narrow white column rises from near the back left corner of the rug off the top edge of the painting. The wall behind the two people and the spaces in the room beyond, to our left, are loosely painted but with strokes that suggest geometric or lattice-like patterns. The artist signed the painting near the lower left: “Boldini.”

This painting shows a woman seated on a wooden chair outside. She is turned to the left, and we see her in profile. She holds a white cloth in her hands and looks down at it. The woman has pale skin and dark hair styled in a bun on the top of her head, and her legs are crossed. She wears a dress with a white bodice and pink skirt. There is a small hoop earring in her ear and a bracelet on her wrist. On the ground by her feet is another piece of white fabric. She sits by a large tree on the right side of the painting and is surrounded by green leaves and yellow grass. Small areas of blue sky are visible through the canopy of leaves above her. Behind her, the roof and side of a building are visible.
Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase and Gift of William A. Clark, 1918)

This painting depicts a river crossing.  In the center of the painting, a horse-drawn carriage is at the river's edge. The carriage itself is on the right, the wheels still partially submerged in the water, while on the left the four horses are climbing up into the bank. The horses appear to be in distress, rearing up onto their back legs and raising their heads into the air. A man on the shore is trying to calm them down, his hands raised upwards. Behind the man, on the left side of the painting, is an abandoned fishing rod and basket, and a small brown dog appears to chew one of the fishing lines. The people in the carriage - two women in dresses and feathered hats and two men in dark uniforms with gold details - look towards the horses with wide eyes and open, downturned mouths. At the base of the carriage, there is a man in a blue coat standing in the water, grasping the long reins of the horses. A black top hat floats near him on the shore. On the right, another dog stands in the water, facing the carriage. Behind it, men in a long wooden boat help a man who is submerged in the water, lifting him up towards the boat. In the distance, behind the carriage, three people can be seen on the opposite bank of the river, their hands raised. All of the people in the painting have light skin. The carriage is bright yellow against the blue-gray water, and the shore on the left is a strip of brown dirt with small gray pebbles that leads into dark green grass. On the left and right, the bank is lined with tall, dark green trees. The horizon shows green hills and a distant light-blue mountain range. The sky is pale blue with white clouds tinged with peach, and the water beneath it reflects these colors.
Plate with an allegorical scene of a woman and a putto

This is a painting on a ceramic plate of a mythological scene featuring a cherub and a reclining nude figure with a background of a landscape and buildings. The scene is richly colored with a vibrant palette, including deep blues, greens, and earth tones, depicting a landscape with a river or body of water, a tree, and classical-style architecture. The cherubic figure with colorful wings holds a bow, while the reclining figure is partially draped in orange fabric. This imagery is set on a round ceramic surface, likely a piece of Italian maiolica from the Renaissance period. This is in style of an anonymous Renaissance pottery artist, referencing both classical themes and decorative ceramics.
Plate with the Plague of Phrygia

This is a painting of a narrative scene on a circular ceramic plate. The plate is decorated with intricate and colorful imagery depicting various figures and animals engaged in different activities. In the foreground, there is a central pedestal with an inscription, surrounded by various characters and animals, including a bovine figure on the left and a variety of other figures interacting with each other, some appearing to be sleeping or in distress. The scene is bustling with activity, with architectural elements and lush greenery in the background.

This painting depicts a green field of cotton plants with white blossoms. Three individuals are seen harvesting the cotton. They appear to be wearing skirts and bonnets and have dark skin, although their faces aren’t detailed. The background includes buildings on the left and green trees against a pale blue sky with hints of grey. The painting utilizes loose, visible brushstrokes. The color scheme is warm and natural, featuring shades of green, brown, and muted tones.
Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Josephine Boardman Crane, 1957)
Plate with Marsyas and his companions

This is a painting of a pastoral scene with figures around a central tree on a circular ceramic dish. The image depicts several nude and partially draped classical figures in a lush landscape. At the center, a figure is playing a lute, surrounded by others who appear to be listening or engaging in their own activities. The background includes greenery, distant architectural structures, a body of water, and a sky with soft clouds. This is in the style of Renaissance art.
Rustic Plate with Shells, Water Creatures, and Dragonfly

This is a photograph of an ornate ceramic platter. The surface of the platter is detailed with natural motifs, such as leaves, fruits, and small creatures like a snail and insects. In the center, there is a concentric circular design, surrounded by textures resembling wood and stone. The dominant colors are earthy greens and browns, with touches of blues, reds, and whites. The overall design captures the intricacies of nature in a three-dimensional form, showcasing pottery and ceramic glazing techniques.
Nearing the Issue at the Cockpit

This painting shows a group of men gathered closely together, leaning over a wooden railing with their hands resting on it. The men are dressed in various attire including top hats, bowler hats, and flat caps, with a range of semi-formal to casual clothing such as black suits, brown coats, and plain shirts. They are a diverse group, with skin tones ranging from pale to dark brown, some with mustaches or beards and other bare faced. They all appear to be focused intently on something that is just below us, some with slight smiles, others with wide eyes and raised brows. The background includes a wooden beam ceiling and a partially peeling plaster wall with a framed document labeled "RULES" partially visible near the upper right. On the upper left, the graying plaster appears to have cracked off, revealing red brick.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
Albarello with black-bearded physician and trophies of arms

The image depicts a ceramic pharmacy jar with a detailed portrayal of a man with a dark beard and a white turban, appearing to read a script. The sculpture is made from ceramics and features vivid colors such as yellows, blues, and greens. The upper and lower bands of the jar have alternating horizontal stripes of yellow and blue, while the central band showcases ornate designs including leafy wreaths and stylized floral motifs. The jar gives the impression of an elaborately decorated, traditional apothecary vessel, finely painted with intricate patterns and an illustration for historical context.

The sculpture is a bust of a male figure. It features detailed, curly hair and a strong facial expression with prominent cheekbones and a straight nose. The sculpture is predominantly dark in color, indicating it might be made from bronze or a similar metal material. The bust includes shoulders and is mounted on a round pedestal base. Its size and positioning suggest it is slightly above eye level. The high polish of the material reflects light, highlighting the intricacies of the hair and facial features.

The sculpture depicts a panther in a walking pose, with its head lowered and one paw partially raised. It is intricately detailed within a rectangular frame, exhibiting a sense of movement. Made of bronze, it has a greenish patina. The panther is shown in low relief, slightly raised against the background. The frame surrounding the sculpture is of the same material and coloration, with decorative elements at the top center.

This painting depicts a street scene from a slightly elevated perspective. A tan dirt road stretches into the distance, lined with white houses on the left side. On the right side is a tall fence, and behind it the green tops of trees or bushes are visible. People in dark clothing walk along the street in the distance. Beyond them, taller trees are visible, with more buildings below them. The sky above is softly colored in hues of yellow, peach, and gray. The brushstrokes are loose and visible.
Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
Tile with Saint Martin and the Begger

This is a painting of a medieval scene on a ceramic tile. The tile features a central image of a figure on horseback dressed in a green robe, reaching out with a red cloth towards another figure beside the horse. This second figure is on foot, draped in a similar red cloth. The horse appears dynamic and detailed, standing on a grassy landscape with a few stylized trees and architectural elements in the background. The outer edge is adorned with an intricate repeating pattern in orange tones, while the edges of the tile display a blue border with geometric designs. This is in the style of traditional Maiolica ware, a type of tin-glazed pottery.

The sculpture is a bust depicting a female figure with classical features and a serene gaze. Her hair is intricately carved in waves and tied back. It is made of white marble with a polished finish. The bust ends at the shoulders with draped clothing featuring gentle folds and texture. The simple marble stand supports the sculpture.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1873)

This painting depicts a coastal scene with a large group of people with light skin dressed in draping fabric in shades of red, yellow, blue, and purple. In the bottom left corner, two men, one old and one young, stand in front of a dark, stormy sea, upon which a large ship is tilting dramatically to one side near large, rocky cliffs. The sky above the ship is full of dark clouds, with streaks of bright yellow surrounded by magenta breaking through the gray. The men face the right, and the young man has his hand outstretched towards a group of women in a grassy meadow dotted with small flowers. One woman at the front of the group faces the men, her arm outstretched towards them. Three women sit at her feet, and a group of five women cluster behind her, hugging one another tightly. On the right, four more women dance in a group, their arms upraised and knees bent. Behind the meadow are tall, olive-green trees.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Bernice West Beyers, 1963)
Charger with the Massacre of the Innocents

This is a painting of a scene with classical figures and architecture on a ceramic plate. The central focus is a pedestal with two statuesque figures, surrounded by multiple human figures engaged in various activities. The background shows architectural structures against a colorful sky. The figures and elements are rendered in a rich color palette with an emphasis on blues, greens, and golden hues, creating a sense of drama and movement typical of Renaissance art. This is in the style of Renaissance Italian maiolica, depicting historical and mythological scenes with intricate detail and vibrant colors.

The portrait depicts a man standing with one hand resting on a blue fabric covered table. He has a dignified posture, relaxed shoulders, and a calm facial expression. He has fair skin, a rounded face, grayish-white hair styled in curls typical of the 18th century. The man is dressed in a dark coat with decorative buttons and wide-cuffed sleeves showing white ruffled cuffs. He wears a white cravat. The background includes a stone column and a view of a landscape with a blue sky, hills, clouds, and trees.
Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, William A. Clark Fund and Anna E. Clark Fund, 1965)

The sculpture is a bust depicting an adult male with a mustache and wavy hair swept to the sides. The subject's expression is calm, with closed lips and slightly downcast eyes. He is draped in a robe that is intricately carved to capture the folds of the fabric. The sculpture is made of white marble, giving it a pristine appearance. It is set against a plain background.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1877)

The painting depicts four boys, sitting or leaning against boxes, a wooden platform, and a stone wall. The boy on the left is sitting on the wooden platform, leaning back with his legs crossed, and wearing a blue shirt, brown pants, and a wide-brimmed hat. Next to him, standing on the same platform and sitting on stacked boxes, are two of the other boys. One of these boys is wearing light-colored trousers and a buttoned-up vest underneath a light-colored jacket. The other boy stands slightly behind him, dressed in a red shirt, a dark vest, and a dark jacket, with a brown hat. The last boy, standing to the right and leaning against a low stone wall, is wearing dark-blue trousers, a brown jacket, and a wide-brimmed straw hat. All of the boys have brown skin and short, dark hair. The background showcases a bustling harbor scene with numerous docked sailing ships, buildings, and equipment, all under a pale gray sky.
Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund and William A. Clark Fund, 1960)

The image shows a decorative round plate with elaborate black and yellow scrollwork, a central emblem, and a scene of figures engaged in various activities. The color palette includes vibrant yellows, greens, blues, and earth tones. Detailed designs with the emblem in the center, figures along the lower edge, and a colorful banner with text at the top of the plate.

The sculpture is of a young woman with her head turned slightly to the side and downward. Her hair is styled back into a bun, and her facial features are delicately rendered with smooth lines and contours. The sculpture is made from white marble, giving it a polished appearance. It shows the bust from just below the shoulders, including the upper torso, with a suggested drape texture. The figure appears calm and serene, with lifelike details carved into the marble, such as the curve of her shoulders and the depiction of her facial features and hair.
Study for "Breton Women at a Pardon"
The image shows a man in a formal outfit and a calm expression.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1879)

The sculpture depicts a woman standing with one hand on her hip and the other holding a small round object, while a bird or small animal perches on her shoulder. She seems to be leaning on a tall object on the right, which her bent elbow rests on. The woman is dressed in a draped gown that falls elegantly to her feet, with detailed folds in the fabric. Her skin is mostly white, with some patches of brown, and her reddish-brown hair is intricately styled on top of her head. Her outfit, the object she holds, and the creature on her shoulder are all blends of white, reddish-brown, and light brown pigments. The sculpture stands on a flat rectangular base.

The sculpture depicts a panther in motion, portrayed with a muscular and sleek form. It is made of dark bronze with a smooth and polished finish, featuring highlights that give a subtle sheen. The panther is placed on a textured base resembling rocky terrain, appearing life-like in a prowling pose. The details showcase the muscles and fluid lines, conveying a realistic and artistically crafted representation of the animal in motion.

The sculpture depicts a reclining deer-like animal on a rectangular base. The animal's head is slightly turned to the side, with ears perked up and body resting comfortably. The sculpture is rendered in patinated bronze, exhibiting a combination of green and dark brown hues. The sculpture is relatively small and fits on a flat, stepped base. The texture of the animal's fur is suggested through subtle, uneven surfaces.
Plate with an allegorical scene of Calliope and a youth (from the Ladder Service)

This is a painting of a classical architectural scene with figures. The image depicts a woman seated in an architectural setting decorated with columns and arches, alongside a kneeling child and another figure holding a sphere. The painting is highly detailed, with the architectural setting resembling a palatial interior, complete with checkered flooring and intricate brickwork. The columns are painted in a vibrant blue hue, and the background features a view of a blue sky and distant buildings. The seated woman appears to be interacting with the kneeling child, possibly teaching or bestowing wisdom, as indicated by the open book and laurel wreath. The third figure, dressed in robes and holding the sphere, contributes to the scholarly or philosophical theme of the scene.
Dish with Orpheus charming the beasts

This is a painting of a pastoral scene on a ceramic plate. It depicts a nude figure seated on a rocky landscape, holding a stringed musical instrument and a staff or spear. The background shows a lush landscape with hills, rocks, a stream, and a village with castle-like structures. The sky has a gradient from yellow to blue with clouds. In the foreground, a rabbit sits on a rock. The painting features a blend of blue, green, and earth tones in the style of early Renaissance Italian majolica with classical themes.
Plate with Saint Paul preaching at Athens

This is a painting of a gathering in an architectural setting. The composition features figures dressed in flowing robes around a temple or public square. One central figure is gesturing dynamically, possibly addressing the assembly or leading a discussion. The background shows classical architecture with columns, arches, and a statue of an armored figure. The scene is enclosed within a circular frame. The colors are vivid, with blues, oranges, and earth tones predominating the palette. This is in the style of Raphael, owing to the classical theme and details of the architecture and clothing.

The sculpture depicts a standing female figure holding an object in her hands, which appears curved around her body and extends from her side. Her attire is characterized by draped cloth. The figure features a large headdress with intricate detailing. The sculpture is primarily made of a material resembling terracotta, with natural earthen colors of orange, brown, and some white areas. The finish is rough-textured with visible signs of aging, giving it an ancient appearance. The overall form and posture resemble classical sculpture styles.

The sculpture depicts a standing figure of a female holding a fan in one hand. The figure is dressed in classical attire with a draped garment that covers the body. It is made of terracotta, evident by its earthy reddish-brown color with lighter areas suggesting weathering or patina. The sculpture's form is slightly elongated and slim, with an emphasis on the pleats and folds of the garment, adding to the sense of flow and movement. The sculpture appears antiquated and weathered, giving it a sense of age and historical presence.

The sculpture depicts a panther in a poised, walking stance, with its head turned slightly to the side and mouth open. The panther is crafted from a dark material, possibly bronze, giving it a shiny appearance. The sculpture rests on a rectangular base that elevates the panther slightly.

The relief features a deer in mid-motion, its legs outstretched as if it is running or leaping through grass. It is made of a dark metallic material with a verdigris patina. The deer is depicted in profile, detailed with a focus on its muscular form and the texture of its fur, frozen in a dynamic and lively movement. It is set within a structured rectangular frame with ornate elements at the top corners, enhancing the overall classical appearance of the piece. The relief is flat and suggests it is meant to be viewed as a wall-mounted art piece.
Figurine of a Veiled Dancer with Tambourine

The sculpture depicts a figure in flowing robes holding a round object. The material is light-colored, possibly terracotta, with a combination of pale earthy hues and areas of wear exposing a natural base color underneath. The figure's head is slightly tilted to the side, with facial features barely discernible, encased in fabric or hair. The sculpture stands upright with a sturdy base and has a textured, aged appearance.

The sculpture depicts a mounted figure in military attire, sitting atop a horse. The figure is a man dressed in a uniform with decorative details including a prominent hat, shoulder epaulettes, and a sash across his chest. The man holds the reins with one hand and is looking forward with a composed expression. The horse is portrayed mid-stride with its front right leg raised. The sculpture is crafted in a dark bronze material and set on a rectangular base.

The sculpture is a bronze medallion with a profile relief of a man's head and shoulders facing left. The man has short, neatly combed hair, a prominent nose, and a thoughtful expression. The medallion is circular with a detailed texture, enhancing its three-dimensional depth. It features the inscription "INAUGURATION - MARCH 4, 1929." The bronze color catches light, highlighting the embossed figure's contours. The medallion appears to be handheld or displayed as a collectible item.

The sculpture depicts a female figure holding a large circular object, likely a tambourine, with both hands. The figure is adorned in a flowing garment that drapes around her body, emphasizing the curves and folds of the fabric. The sculpture is primarily colored in shades of off-white and brown, with remnants of paint. It appears to be crafted from terracotta and stands on a small rounded base. The figure's serene expression and detailed garment texture suggest a classic representation of historical statuary.

The sculpture depicts a fawn lying down on a textured surface. The fawn has a slender body, large ears, and a small tail. It is crafted from bronze with green patina highlights. The sculpture captures the posture and expression of the animal. It is mounted on an oval stone base.

The sculpture depicts a seated figure of a woman wearing a turban-like headpiece. She holds a scepter in her right hand and her left hand is open. She wears a robe that covers her feet and holds an open book. The figure is seated on a throne with decorative elements. The sculpture is made of dark bronze with an aged patina. It is presented frontally and centrally.
Corcoran Collection (Anonymous gift in memory of Helen Minshall, 1955)

The sculpture depicts a seated female figure holding a sword, with one hand raised to her forehead. She is placed on a textured base and made of a dark material, likely bronze, with a green patina. The woman's body is detailed and lifelike, with bare feet resting on the base. The statue conveys a sense of strength and contemplation.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Joan B. Detweiler, 1962)

This is a photograph of a decorative ceramic plate featuring an intricate design with concentric circles. The plate has a central motif of two hands shaking, surrounded by blue, orange, and white colors and various geometric patterns. The inner border has zigzag and triangular shapes, while the outer border alternates between blue and orange segments. The plate includes an inscription "FIL FEL" on a blue ribbon-like band. The design suggests a traditional or historical style of pottery.

The sculpture depicts a bear standing on its hind legs with its front paws raised and slightly bent. The bear's head is slightly tilted, showing detailed facial features and fur texture. The sculpture is made of bronze with a patinated surface, and the bear stands on a base resembling natural terrain.

The sculpture depicts a small angel figure with wings, embracing a head or spherical shape with arms wrapped around it. It is made from terracotta material with an earthy reddish-brown color. The angel stands on a small platform. Its facial features and wings are outlined with softness. The size of the sculpture is roughly that of a small figurine or decorative piece.

The sculpture depicts a relief of a large cat in profile as it walks or prowls sideways. It is crafted from green-colored material, likely oxidized bronze, giving it a slightly mottled appearance with variations of darker and lighter green. The feline's form is carved into a rectangular plaque set within a framed structure. The frame has a green patina matching the central relief. Two decorative elements resembling ornamental finials are symmetrically placed on top of the frame. The overall appearance is flat with the feline figure distinct yet integrated into the surrounding material.
Oinochoe in the Form of a Female Head

The sculpture features the head of a figure with stylized facial features including almond-shaped eyes, a slightly smiling mouth, and a prominent nose. The head is topped with an elongated neck that transforms into a vessel with a spout. The sculpture is crafted from a material that appears to be ceramic or terracotta, with muted colors including light brown, beige, and traces of black and red. Some areas show signs of wear or fading. The sculpted head sits on a flat base, making it stand upright.

The sculpture depicts a reclining dog, resembling a greyhound, on a rectangular base. The dog's body is detailed, showcasing strong, defined muscles and the typical sleek form of the breed. The sculpture is made of bronze, with a dark, metallic color and highlights suggesting a patina. The dog's head is turned to one side, with perked ears, and wears a collar. The sculpture's posture, proportions, and surface texture give it a realistic and poised appearance as it rests.

Three cows drink in a placid body of water in front of a landscape dim with golden sunset light in this horizontal painting. The water creates white eddies around a few rocks as it travels from the lower left corner of the canvas, across the foreground, and off to the right. In the bottom right quadrant of the composition, one cow is white, and another dark brown. The third, tawny brown cow flicks her tail as she dips her head to the water. Tall groves of trees on the far side of the water fill most of the right half of the composition. To the left, a path curves from the waterside back into a grassy, tree-pocked landscape with buildings on one low hill and a very distant horizon, which comes halfway up this composition. A person wearing a red vest over a white long-sleeved shirt, dark blue, knee-length pants, and a brown, brimmed hat rides a white horse coming toward us on the path. A short-hair, pale gray dog runs ahead of the horse, toward the cows. From below the horizon, the sunlight sets the grassy fields to golden tan, and the sky above fades from buttery yellow along the horizon to pale blue along the top of the composition. Lines of clouds are lit mauve pink and shaded ultramarine blue.
Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, William A. Clark Fund, Gallery Fund, and gifts of Orme Wilson, George E. Hamilton, Jr., and R. M. Kauffmann, 1963)

The sculpture shows a dog lying down with its body slightly curled and its head on its front legs. The material of the sculpture appears to be bronze with a dark, greenish-brown patina. The details of the dog's muscular structure and fur texture are intricately captured. It is mounted on an oval base, with the dog's body stretched out horizontally.

The sculpture depicts a standing human figure draped in a flowing garment that wraps around the body and covers the head. This figure appears to be in a relaxed stance, and part of the garment is delicately drawn over one shoulder while the rest of the fabric seems to hang in soft folds. The sculpture is predominantly a light, creamy beige with subtle hints of reddish-brown tones. The piece is crafted from a material that appears to be a form of terracotta or stone. Its size relative to us appears diminutive, as suggested by the level of detail and the small base on which it stands. The surface of the sculpture is textured.

This is a painting on a ceramic plate depicting a wooded landscape with figures. The scene features tall trees, mountains, and a clear sky. In the foreground, there are four figures; two playing musical instruments and the other two interacting dynamically. The figures have classical poses and expressions. The colors used are mainly greens, blues, and earth tones. The scene evokes themes of nature, music, and possibly mythology or romantic interaction. The style is influenced by the Italian Renaissance, with a focus on harmonious compositions and mythological themes.

The sculpture depicts an elk struggling with two wolves, one on its neck. The elk is shown in motion with its mouth open. The surface is textured to represent fur and terrain. The sculpture is dark-colored, likely bronze, giving it a polished finish. The animals appear life-sized, conveying realism and detail.

The sculpture depicts a stag with prominent antlers standing over two resting deer, one on each side. The animals show a naturalistic and graceful appearance. The sculpture is primarily a dark metallic color, likely made of a material such as bronze. The stag stands above the other two deer, which are laying down on a textured base. The surface of the sculpture is smooth and slightly reflective, with detailed texturing defining the animals' fur and musculature. The composition captures a moment of interaction among the animals, oriented towards the viewer.

The sculpture shows a seated nude female figure wearing a blindfold. She holds an upright staff in one hand and is seated on a rock-like formation. It is crafted from a dark bronze material, giving it a deep greenish-black color with a slight patina on some surfaces. The sculpture is slightly smaller than life-size relative to human proportions and is mounted on a round, polished base.

The sculpture shows a large, muscular cat-like predator positioned over a smaller prey animal. The predator's posture is low and captures the moment of capture. Both animals are made of a dark, metallic material like bronze. The sculpture emphasizes the power and grace of the predator through detailed form and a smooth texture. The base is rough and complements the natural setting. The details convey a realistic encounter in nature.

The sculpture depicts a horse in motion with its front left leg raised and its head turned to the side. It is crafted from a dark, metallic material with a green patina. The horse's muscles and contours are detailed, and it stands on a rocky base.
Artemis or Bendis with a Herm of Pan

The sculpture features a resting big cat depicted in a curled-up pose on an oval base. The sculpture is made from a dark-colored material, likely bronze, with subtle green patination visible in areas. The detailing of the sculpture captures the animal's fur texture and muscular structure. The sculpture is positioned at an angle that allows viewers to see the animal's head and body. The base upon which the animal rests is textured.

The sculpture depicts a lion with a regal presence. The lion sits upright with its body facing slightly to the right and its head turned to the left. The mane is detailed and cascades over its neck and shoulders. The sculpture is made of a dark material, likely bronze, with a greenish patina. The lion is seated on an oval-shaped base.
The sculpture depicts a lion facing the left, its mouth slightly open and its tail curving. It is a dark metallic color with a glossy sheen. The sculpture is placed on a rectangular base.

The sculpture depicts two lions engaged in a fierce interaction. It is made of bronze with touches of green patina. The lions are finely crafted with intricate details in their manes and muscular bodies, capturing their dynamic movement and tension. The sculpture is set on a round base and is approximately the size of a small table centerpiece.

The sculpture depicts a large feline, resembling a panther or lioness, standing on a textured base. It is crafted from dark bronze material, giving it an almost black appearance with subtle reflections. The animal is shown in a poised stance with its tail elegantly curved, showcasing precise attention to anatomical details.

The sculpture depicts a feline, resembling a panther, in a lying position. It is made of dark green material, similar to bronze. The surface is textured and reflects light. The panther has its front paws stretched out, head slightly turned, and tail curling. The facial features show an attentive expression. It sits on an oval base of the same material. The sculpture portrays a lifelike, detailed representation of the animal.

The sculpture depicts a reclining panther with its front paws extended, body slightly turned to one side. The panther's form is meticulously crafted with details like its head and body structure. The sculpture is made of dark bronze, giving it an aged patina with hints of greenish undertones. The panther exudes a sense of calm strength and lays on a rocky base engraved with the name "BARYE." The sculpture is small, meant for close viewing to appreciate its craftsmanship and representation of the animal's grace.

The sculpture depicts a bird in a standing position with a long tail extending behind it. The bird is detailed with distinct feathers and a beak. The color of the sculpture is a greenish-bronze, indicating a metal material, likely bronze with a patina. It is mounted on a rectangular base that matches the sculpture's color and material. The form of the sculpture is realistic yet stylized, capturing the essence of the bird with elegance and attention to detail.

The sculpture is of a horse's head. It captures details such as the ears, eyes, nostrils, and a slightly open mouth. The sculpture is made of dark metal, likely bronze, with a green patina. It has a textured and aged appearance. The sculpture is presented in profile view, emphasizing the contours and musculature of the horse's neck and head, as well as the intricately carved mane along the top. The naturalistic portrayal of the horse's features gives the sculpture a lifelike and dynamic presence.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1958)

The sculpture features a bird in flight with its wings extended upward. It is crafted from dark green material, likely patinated bronze, giving it a textured appearance. The bird is depicted in a side profile, showcasing its wingspan and feather patterns. It sits on an uneven base resembling a natural element. The sheen on the material highlights the bird's anatomy, providing a realistic representation.

The sculpture depicts a scene with a panther confronting a deer. The panther appears dominant, standing over the prey with its powerful body and muscular form clearly illustrated. The color of the sculpture varies from dark brown to greenish hues, possibly due to the patina that has developed on the bronze material. The scene is captured with realism in the surface details, such as the fur texture and the tension in the panther's stance. The size of the sculpture suggests it is a table-top piece, allowing viewers to closely observe the intricate craftsmanship of this depiction of a predator and its prey.
Candlestick, Greek Style with Antique Medallions

The sculpture is a decorative candlestick with a portrait medallion of a man with curly hair on its central stem. It is crafted from dark metal with a greenish hue, featuring ornate design details including fluted stem, floral and leaf patterns on the circular base, and intricate embossed decorations on the candle holder section. The sculpture stands firmly on a base, exuding stability and timeless design.
Antique Style Three Light Candelabra with Chains

The sculpture depicts a candelabra that is made of dark-colored metal, likely bronze, with a patina giving it an aged appearance. It features a stand with candle holders at the top, ornamental figures resembling mythical creatures, intricate scrollwork, and chains draping from the holders. The design is sophisticated and detailed, showcasing a blend of artistic elements.

The sculpture is a candelabrum with two arms extending from a central stem. The candelabrum is made of greenish material, likely patinated metal. The central section of the sculpture has intricate openwork with curved, symmetrical designs. The arms of the candelabrum are elegantly curved and have small, round holders for candles. The base is wide and circular, providing stability. The piece exhibits detailed craftsmanship with ornamental patterns enhancing its classical and antique aesthetic.

The sculpture portrays three dogs in a dynamic encounter on a rocky base. The dogs have muscular physiques and are shown in action. The central dog is dominant, rearing up with its mouth open. Another dog is lying on its back, and the third dog is standing upright and lunging forward. The sculpture is made from a dark material, likely bronze, giving it a rich brown color with a metallic sheen. The surface detailing captures the texture of the dogs' fur and muscles realistically.
Lion of the Column of July

The sculpture depicts a lion in profile, striding in a regal manner. The material used is dark, possibly bronze. The lion's mane is intricately detailed against the smoother body texture. In the background are five stars in relief. The artist's name, "BARYE," is inscribed at the bottom right. The sculpture is presented in a rectangular plaque format.
Figurine of a Goddess (possibly Aphrodite) or a Woman, Leaning on an Ionic Column

The sculpture depicts a standing female figure draped in a long flowing garment. The texture is slightly rough, with remnants of a pale white and beige finish. The material seems to be terracotta, showing signs of wear and age. The figure has a classical pose with one hand on her hip and the other potentially interacting with an unseen object. The head is proportional to the body, displaying delicate facial features. Some details on the head are reduced due to wear. The sculpture is mounted on a rectangular base.

The sculpture depicts a scene of a large feline dominating a smaller combatant. The feline is poised above its prey, with its body tense and muscles defined. The sculpture is made of darkly patinated bronze, giving it an earthy appearance. The piece captures a moment frozen in time, allowing viewers to observe the details of the animals' forms and the interaction.

The sculpture depicts a horse standing with its head lowered. The sculpture is made of bronze and has a dark, metallic brown color with a slight sheen. The horse is sculpted in a realistic manner, with attention to musculature and anatomical details, like the mane and tail. The sculpture is mounted on a rectangular base. The overall design captures the natural pose and form of a horse.

The sculpture shows a lion attacking a horse. The lion has its claws on the horse's back as the horse rears back. The piece is made of dark bronze with a metallic sheen. It is highly detailed, showing the muscles and movement of both animals accurately. The base looks like rugged ground. The sculpture is medium-sized, ideal for viewing from various angles.
Molded dish with Joseph's robe being presented to his father

This is a painting on ornamental pottery. The artwork is on a decorative ceramic plate depicting a scene within an arched architectural setting. The detailed artwork includes elements of Renaissance-era attire and architectural forms. The background features a brick archway, buildings, and a blue sky with clouds. In the foreground, a group of figures is gathered in a dynamic arrangement. The figures are dressed in colorful period costumes, with one figure seated on an ornate chair. Rich drapery in blue and white stripes hangs on the right side. This style is reminiscent of Renaissance majolica ware, known for its vivid colors and narrative scenes.
Ephebe in Traveling Hat, Cloak, and Boots

The sculpture depicts a standing figure draped in a long robe, with a portion of the garment wrapped over one shoulder. The subject of the sculpture is a male figure, indicated by the short hair and facial features. The material of the sculpture is a type of stone or ceramic with an earthy tone primarily grayish-brown in color, with subtle hints of pink and white showing remnants of original paint. On top of the figure's head is a flat, hat-like object. The sculpture stands on a rectangular base, with the figure's left arm resting on a column-like support. The sculpture displays a sense of balance and stability, with details in the drapery and posture suggesting a classical influence in its design.
Plate with the Triumph of Bacchus

This is a painting of a mythological scene on a decorative plate. The scene depicted involves several figures engaged in an active, dynamic composition. The central figure is supported or carried by several other figures along a landscape filled with vibrant colors, including greens, blues, and warm earth tones. The background features an idyllic landscape with trees and rocky formations under a sky exhibiting gradations of blue and orange hues. A figure to the left appears to be playing a musical instrument. This is in the style of Renaissance majolica pottery, encompassing mythological and classical themes painted with vivid colors on ceramic ware.
Cupid, Stung by a Bee, Is Cherished by his Mother

A seated woman wrapped in a spruce-blue garment embraces a tearful, winged boy in this round painting. Both have smooth, pale skin with flushed cheeks, delicate features, and golden-brown hair. The woman takes up most of the painting. She sits angled to our left as she curls both arms around the nearly nude boy, Cupid. Her hair is plaited at the back of her head behind a blue-green headband. The upper arm we can see is encircled with a gold band set with blue gems, and one breast is bare in the shadow over her crooked elbow. The other hand holds the boy’s middle finger. Cupid’s body faces our right, toward the woman, but he turns back to look at the hand the woman holds. His other hand is lifted to his eyes, and a tear gleams on one cheek. His body is covered only by a white cloth that crosses his chest and covers his genitals. A silvery-white and tawny-gold wing juts out behind one shoulder. The woman sits on a pillowy rust-red cushion. One gray dove feeds another at Cupid’s feet, and a pink rose lies nearby. A field of olive green and mustard yellow suggests a tree behind Cupid and the woman. In the distance to our left, three pale-skinned, chubby babies tussle with mouths wide open in a garden near a beehive. Bees teem out of the conical hive. Peach-colored clouds skim the muted blue sky above. The artist signed and dated the lower left, “B. West 1774.”
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Bernice West Beyers, 1963)
Landscape Woman Death Tree Mourning Dove Urn Memorial

This is a painting depicting a figure in mourning beside a memorial. The figure is leaning against a tombstone with an urn atop, surrounded by weeping willows. The tombstone is inscribed with a message— "Died 24 Jan, 1805 Aged 18 Months Blessed Spirit Rest in Peace". The willow branches frame the scene, and the figure's long dress and lowered gaze express contemplation and grief. The landscape features greenery under a serene sky, contributing to the somber atmosphere.

The sculpture depicts a bear in a seated position, tending to its front paw with a lifted hind leg. It is crafted from a dark material, likely bronze, with a textured surface that emphasizes the bear's fur. The sculpture stands on a rounded base.
Mantel Clock with Chariot of the Grape Harvest
gilded bronze, enamel on copper, and Verde de Mer marble

The sculpture features a decorative clock with a classical theme, composed of several figures and elements. The central subject is a woman in a flowing draped garment, seated on a chariot-like structure. She holds a large branch or scepter, while an infant figure stands beside her with an object in its hand. The chariot is pulled by a lion, sculpted with detailed features. A winged cherub or small figure is depicted guiding the lion with reins. The ensemble is crafted from gilded bronze. The clock face is white with black numerals and hands, located beneath the seated woman. The base of the sculpture is dark green with gold accents and patterns, supported by four small structures.
Ten-Point Stag Brought Down by Two Scotch Hounds

The sculpture depicts a scene of multiple animals engaged in a struggle or chase. The central figure is a large stag with antlers, being attacked by three wolves. One wolf is on the stag's back, another is biting its side, and the third is below. The stag's mouth is open. The sculpture appears dark in color, likely bronze, with a patinated finish emphasizing the animals' textures. The piece is mounted on a tiered base. The intricate details make the animals appear lifelike and highly detailed.
Fragment of a Statue of a Young Man
Albarello with woman spinning and putti on sea monsters

This is a photograph of a decorative ceramic vase. The vase has painted scenes and motifs across its surface. The upper portion features a seated figure, peacock-like designs, foliage, and an orange color amidst green leaves. The middle section has an inscription reading "FILIONIO." The bottom section depicts cherubs or putti, one riding on a dolphin-like creature over waves. The composition suggests an ornate, historical style, possibly reminiscent of Italian Renaissance ceramics known for vivid colors and detailed storytelling in art.
The Arcadian Shepherds (Et in Arcadia ego) [obverse]

This sculpture is a round golden medallion with a detailed design carved in relief. The scene on the medallion features four people standing and kneeling in front of a large rectangular object that looks like a monument or tombstone. Three of the people wear togas and hold long objects with curved ends, and two of them have circlets of leaves over their short hair. The fourth person on the right wears a long, draped garment and a cloth covering over their long hair. They look to the left, towards what the other three are doing. Surrounding the group are several tall trees. The medallion's edge has a beaded border for decoration. Inscribed at the bottom are the words "ET AMENT MEMINISSE PERITI," with a smaller line of text below them.
The Indiana Medal (The Admission of Indiana to the Union) [obverse]

The sculpture is a circular relief medallion featuring two figures. The central subject is a robed figure holding a torch in her right hand. Beside her is a smaller figure standing on a pedestal reaching towards the torch. The figures are depicted in a classical style, with the larger figure dressed in a draped garment. The medallion is bronze in color, suggesting it is made from a metal like bronze. The border of the medallion has an intricate, woven pattern. Inscribed to the right of the figures are the words "THE ADMISSION OF INDIANA TO THE UNION." The sculpture is detailed and skillfully rendered.

The image shows a circular ceramic relief sculpture depicting a central scene surrounded by a written inscription. The sculpture features a religious or spiritual scene set within an arched area resembling a bed or altar. The setting includes figures in period attire gathered around a central figure lying down. Above them, another figure is depicted within a cloud or floatation device. The colors used include greens, blues, yellows, and whites, with a contrast found in glazed ceramic works. The composition is encircled by a band of text in raised relief, bordered by a rim combining orange and green hues. The material appears to be ceramic or earthenware, with a glossy finish and decorative coating associated with glazed pottery.

The sculpture shows the bust of an elderly woman with detailed facial expressions and signs of aging, such as wrinkles. She wears a headscarf tied over her head and under her chin, with long pieces hanging on either side of her face and a bow tie at the neck. The sculpture is made of bronze and has a dark, weathered patina displaying shades of green and brown. The depiction of facial features and clothing is detailed, creating a realistic and lifelike appearance.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1958)

The sculpture is an ornately decorated pottery vessel with hand-painted images. The main body features a sailing ship on the ocean with clear skies and a few clouds. Surrounding the nautical scene are decorative motifs, including framed portraits of individuals with elaborate hairstyles and attire. The vessel is mostly white with vibrant colors like blue, red, orange, and green used for the detailed imagery. Made out of ceramic, the sculpture appears glossy and smooth, indicative of a glazed finish. The vase has a distinctive lid with a sculpted piece at the top that resembles a grape bunch. The design conveys intricate and delicate craftsmanship.
Christ and the Woman of Samara at the Well

The sculpture features two figures: a seated male with long hair and a beard, and a standing female with long hair and a headdress. The male figure wears a burgundy robe, while the female figure wears a green top and blue skirt. Between them is an ornate green basin with decorative details, including a cherubic face. The male figure rests an arm on the basin and extends the other outward. The female figure stands beside him, holding a jug over the basin as if pouring or filling it. The sculpture is made of glazed ceramic, giving it a glossy finish that enhances the rich colors and details.

The sculpture depicts a woman seated and nursing an infant who is wrapped in swaddling clothes. The woman wears a headscarf and a gown with a blue top and a grayish-blue skirt. The infant is positioned horizontally across her lap, with both hands cradling the baby securely. The sculpture is made from a material that has a glazed, smooth surface. The colors include a creamy tone for both the woman's skin and the baby's swaddling cloth, while the woman’s attire adds a touch of color with its blue and gray shades. The sculpture's life-like size and detail allow us to appreciate the realistic depiction of the maternal subject.
North African Horseman Surprised by a Serpent

The sculpture shows a warrior battling a serpent while mounted on a horse. The serpent is coiled around them both, with intricate scales and a sinuous form. The warrior wields a weapon, partially hidden by the serpent's coils, in a striking pose. The horse rears up, adding movement to the composition. Crafted from bronze, the sculpture has a dark brown color with subtle greenish tones. The medium accentuates the detailed musculature of the horse, the warrior's armor, and the serpent's scales. The scene is frozen at a dramatic moment, encouraging close inspection.

The sculpture depicts a bearded male figure sitting atop a horse-like creature. The figure is partially nude, with his right arm resting on the creature's head. The sculpture is made of ceramic with a glossy finish and is colored in various shades: the man has a flesh-toned complexion with brown hair and beard, while the sea horse is dark brown. The base of the sculpture has green and blue colors, evoking water. The sculpture showcases intricate detailing in the facial features and wavy lines suggesting the creature's mane or scales. It is medium-sized and allows viewers to observe each aspect clearly in a three-dimensional form.

The sculpture depicts a large feline poised over a smaller creature. The panther crouches with one front paw extended towards the smaller animal. The material of the sculpture appears to be bronze, with a greenish-brown hue typical of aged bronze with patina. The metal surface highlights the musculature and fur textures of the animals. The scene is set on a rocky base.

The sculpture depicts a classical female torso. It is missing arms, legs, and a head, focusing solely on the central body from the shoulders to the upper thighs. Crafted from bronze, it exhibits a rich dark green patina with hints of a darker, almost black hue in some areas. The sculpture stands upright on a solid base, with a smooth, highly defined surface. It reflects light subtly, enhancing the musculature and contours of the figure. The piece is life-sized in its proportions.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1958)

The sculpture is a relief portrait of a man with a long, flowing beard and mustache, wearing a wide-brimmed hat. The man's facial features are detailed, capturing his eyes, nose, and the texture of his beard and clothing. The sculpture is circular, giving it a medallion-like appearance. The color of the sculpture is a reddish-brown, suggestive of bronze or a similar metal, with a weathered texture that highlights the details of the relief. The subject appears to be in a three-quarter view, looking slightly to the side, with the name "Walt Whitman" inscribed at the top left edge of the piece. The texture and patina suggest age and a sense of history, while the overall craftsmanship gives a sense of realism and attention to detail.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1958)

The sculpture portrays a male figure in a crouching position. One arm is folded over a bent knee while the other hand rests on the ground. The figure shows detailed muscular features and hair texture. It is made of bronze, giving it a dark, slightly reflective surface. The bronze's texture and patina highlight the human form, accentuating curves and muscles for a lifelike and dynamic appearance. It is mounted on a square bronze base that offers stability and a minimalist aesthetic contrast to the detailed figure.
Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1958)
Dish with a king and a scholar

This is a photograph of a decorative plate with an intricate design. The plate features a central illustration of a regal figure seated on a throne, adorned with a crown and holding a scepter. The figure is accompanied by two smaller figures and appears to be engaged in a scene. Surrounding this scene is a border decorated with intricate patterns and motifs in blue, green, and golden yellow. The design includes elements of florals and abstract shapes, showcasing a harmonious blend of curves and lines. The craftsmanship reflects a style reminiscent of traditional ceramic art from the Renaissance or Medieval periods, likely intended as a functional and ornamental object.

This painting shows a slightly elevated viewpoint looking out across a green landscape towards a reflective body of water. In the green sky, the pale-yellow moon glows brightly, illuminating the scene. At the top of the painting, greenish-yellow clouds with thin brown edges float across the sky. The moonlight reflects off the water, creating a bright pathway at the bottom of the painting. There are the dark silhouettes of trees on the left side, and in the distance the flat green landscape fades into the glowing atmosphere. The colors include muted greens, browns, and golds.

The image shows a miniature portrait of a man's upper body. He is facing forward with his body slightly turned to the right. The man has fair skin, rounded cheeks, and light hair styled in waves away from his face. He wears a dark maroon coat over a white shirt with a white cravat. The portrait is in an oval gold-edged frame against a neutral gray background, suggesting a painted surface with delicate detail.
Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Sarah A. Hagner, 1898)
Drug jar with heads of women

This is a photograph of a decorative ceramic jar with a portrait. The jar is adorned with vibrant colors featuring a central circular medallion depicting a profile portrait. The portrait is done in a classical style, with curly hair, an elaborate ruff collar, and delicate features facing left. The background of the medallion is styled in a warm yellow tone. Surrounding this central image, the jar has intricate patterns in blue, yellow, and green, incorporating leaves and floral motifs. The rounded shape of the jar, along with the rich colors and artistic glaze work, suggest an appreciation for classical art design. The craftsmanship and detail suggest the piece could be from the period of Renaissance ceramics.
Mantel Clock with Diana Hunting in a Chariot
gilded bronze, marble, enamel, and glass

The sculpture features a female figure standing on a chariot drawn by two dogs. She is depicted pulling back on a bow, ready to release an arrow. The sculpture has a golden hue, suggesting it is made of a gilded metal. The base is made of dark-toned stone or marble. The figure’s attire flows naturally, indicating movement. The chariot wheel features an elaborate clock face with Roman numerals on a blue background outlined in gold. The sculpture is mounted on an ornate base decorated with a pattern of gold accents resembling foliage or palmettes.

The sculpture depicts a mounted figure of a man riding a horse. The man is dressed in historical military attire and is holding a sword aloft in his right hand.
